headline: Today's developments feature new AI research spanning video generation agents, robotic manipulation frameworks, and neural network architectures. In industry news, The New York Times warned freelance photographers against updating Adobe Photoshop due to concerns that embedded AI features might incorrectly flag images as AI-generated, while an OpenAI usage reduction item remains unclear due to a lack of details.

items.title: alesha-pro/llm.asm: Qwen3-0.6B inference (12 KB), bare-metal bootable OS (22 KB), and from-scratch Mini-GPT trainer with live Braille TUI (3
items.summary: This repository provides three complete language model projects written entirely in pure x86-64 assembly language, requiring no C, C++, Rust, or external libraries. It includes a static Linux ELF binary for running Qwen3-0.6B inference, a bootable bare-metal OS, and a from-scratch Mini-GPT trainer.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that complex LLM inference, operating systems, and training routines can be implemented entirely in raw assembly language with zero dependencies.

items.title: Much shorter version of GRH Lean verification from Anthropic
items.summary: Researchers produced a shorter version of a Lean 4 formal proof for the Riemann Hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, built in collaboration with Anthropic and Claude. The repository contains two editions of the proof that take between one to two hours to build and have passed machine checks.
items.why_it_matters: It represents a significant automated mathematical verification effort assisted by AI, though the proof has not yet been manually reviewed by human mathematicians.

items.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
items.summary: The New York Times has asked freelance photographers not to use the latest version of Adobe Photoshop due to its embedded AI features. The newsroom is concerned that automated tools and background post-processing will insert C2PA metadata flagging the images as AI-generated, violating editorial standards.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights the friction news organizations face as AI editing capabilities become silently integrated into standard creative software.

items.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), an architecture that reuses shared layers across loops to boost expressivity while maintaining efficiency through selective memory reuse. Pretraining experiments show that a U-shaped variant outperforms baseline models in token efficiency, perplexity, and task accuracy.
items.why_it_matters: This architecture improves the efficiency and performance tradeoffs of looped transformer models, which reuse layers to increase capability.

items.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce PyRUA-Dex, a framework that uses coding agents to develop programmatic policies for dexterous robotic manipulation without requiring human demonstrations. The method involves parallel exploration, code distillation into a task library, and randomized refinement for robustness. In simulation and real-world tests, it achieves top performance on complex bimanual tasks like playing piano and writing calligraphy.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a scalable way for coding agents to teach robots fine-grained manipulation skills entirely from scratch, bypassing the need for scarce human training data.

items.title: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
items.summary: The paper presents VibeVideoAgent, a training-free framework that allows code-driven video generation agents to inspect their media drafts during production. By running multimodal perception in short-lived, separate contexts, the agent evaluates drafts through a set of perception primitives before final rendering. Experiments show that this feedback loop improves audiovisual quality and synchronization across several leading foundation models.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a systematic way for code-writing video agents to catch design errors and synchronization issues early, avoiding costly full-resolution rewrites.

items.title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
items.summary: The authors introduce Agentic LongLive, an asynchronous memory system designed for real-time, long-video generation models. A separate memory agent tracks characters, objects, and scenes using text and image states, feeding contextual data to the video generator ahead of time without slowing down the stream. The system successfully maintains visual consistency over 14-minute stories while operating in real time.
items.why_it_matters: It solves the long-standing problem of maintaining narrative and identity consistency in real-time interactive video streaming without introducing latency.

items.title: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos
items.summary: Researchers present AIRIS, a streaming benchmark designed to evaluate social embodied intelligence through egocentric videos based on Attention, Intention, Reaction, and Interaction. Testing 45 different models, the evaluation reveals that current systems struggle to jointly time their interventions and often guess human intents prematurely. The benchmark provides a diagnostic foundation for improving how AI agents interact socially in real time.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights critical timing and social reasoning flaws in current AI models, helping researchers build safer embodied agents for human environments.

items.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
items.summary: The paper introduces Sage-Med-Preview, a 35-parameter medical multimodal model built using a progressive training curriculum from pretraining to reinforcement learning. Evaluated across numerous clinical tasks and benchmarks, the model outperforms existing open-source medical models and approaches the performance of advanced proprietary systems. The authors share empirical evidence and training recipes to help advance scalable medical AI.
items.why_it_matters: It provides valuable data and training strategies for scaling multimodal AI in the medical domain, where general models often fall short.

items.title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
items.summary: Researchers introduce Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), a method that transfers advanced image editing capabilities to video editors without needing new paired training videos. The technique lets a video editor role-play as an image editor during training by treating single images as one-frame videos. The approach allows models to handle new tasks like action and expression changes on full video clips at test time.
items.why_it_matters: It improves video editing models and expands their capabilities using only individual images, eliminating the need to collect difficult paired video datasets.

items.title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference
items.summary: Nvidia is releasing updates for its Parse 3.5 document model, which turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation and agents. The release includes synthetic training datasets, a fine-tuning recipe, and a speculator tool for faster inference. They also open-sourced three synthetic datasets containing millions of rendered charts, tables, and multilingual OCR documents.
items.why_it_matters: These open-source datasets and fine-tuning recipes give developers resources to build and improve document-parsing and OCR models.

items.title: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: This paper presents Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT), an architecture that reuses network parameters via a weight-shared loop instead of adding more parameters. By dynamically allocating compute across noise levels, the model deepens the network without increasing its parameter count. Experiments show it achieves better generation scores and lower error rates than standard diffusion models while using a fraction of the active parameters.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a more efficient way to scale model capacity and compute for image and text-to-image generation.

items.title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
items.summary: The authors introduce HOG-WAM, a method that improves the visual robustness of world-action models by predicting future Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) during training. An auxiliary module uses structural supervision derived from demonstration images to shape the visual representation used for robot control. The auxiliary module is removed during inference, preserving the standard architecture.
items.why_it_matters: It helps robot control policies perform better under visual noise and corruptions without changing how the model runs at test time.

items.title: Target-Part Preference Optimization for Part-Aware 3D Generation
items.summary: This work explores using preference fine-tuning, specifically Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), to adapt part-aware 3D generators using limited part-annotated data. By ranking candidates generated with different random seeds against ground-truth geometric metrics, the model learns to produce complete and well-separated semantic parts. Experiments on held-out data show that this approach outperforms standard supervised fine-tuning baselines.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a way to improve 3D generation models when high-quality part decompositions are scarce.
